clue.text: Talent shown by Eurovision winner makes German scoff

definitions.note: scoff is British slang for food; a German sausage is German food

parts.note: a knack is a natural talent or skill
Conchita Wurst won the Eurovision Song Contest for Austria in 2014

explanation.surface: A singer's gift for performance earns German approval or ridicule after winning Eurovision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like a verb of mockery; in British slang it is a noun meaning food.
explanation.definitionFit: A knackwurst is a short, fat, spicy sausage from Germany, so it is a German item of food.

clue.text: Enthusiastic to promote new joint

indicators.note: new is abbreviated to its first letter, and promoting it in a down clue lifts that letter higher up the column, earlier in the word

parts.note: keen means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: An eager supporter wants to push for a new joint venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The N for new is lifted from fourth place to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Pale-looking adult enters run-down cinema

indicators.note: the adult's letter goes inside the rearranged word
a run-down building is dilapidated and broken up, so the letters of cinema are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A grown-up walks into a shabby old picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run-down' reads as describing the cinema, but it is what jumbles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia, a shortage of red blood cells, leaves a person pallid, so anaemic is used for pale-looking.

clue.text: Packet Liam and son flourished, they're incorrigible thieves

indicators.note: flourished suggests something waved about with a flourish, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Liam and his son made a packet and thrived, being habitual crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is just a link here; 'son' is taken whole as letters rather than abbreviated to S.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleptomaniacs have a compulsion to steal that they cannot control, hence incorrigible thieves.

clue.text: Practice over, having name higher in draw as outsider?

indicators.note: name is abbreviated to its first letter, and in a down clue putting it higher moves it earlier in the word

parts.note: use means practice or custom
ended means over or finished

explanation.surface: A tennis player whose practice is done hopes to have their name placed higher in the tournament draw.
explanation.walkthrough: The N of ENDED moves up to second place in the combined letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An unseeded player enters a tournament draw without a ranking position, so is regarded as an outsider.

clue.text: Very good opera ultimately that inspires American composer

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the outer letters take in the abbreviation for American

parts.note: so is an adverb meaning very good, as in 'so kind of you'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word opera

parts.note: the final letter of opera
US is short for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A splendid opera finale inspires an American composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' gives US, so the definition is just 'composer'; the surface makes it look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the American bandmaster who wrote marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Decline in cycling once again

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other, as a wheel turns

parts.note: anew means once again

explanation.surface: A cyclist's form is falling off yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of ANEW is moved round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To wane is to diminish or decline, as the moon does after it is full.

clue.text: Publicise trade in deep-sea diving equipment?

parts.note: to air an opinion is to publicise it
a line is a trade or occupation, as in 'what's your line?'

explanation.surface: Advertising a business that sells diving kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a cryptic definition: an air line is the hose feeding a diver air, not a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver's air line is the tube that supplies breathing gas from the surface, read playfully from the word for a carrier company.

clue.text: Put at risk of death, given faulty grenade

parts.note: end is a word for death

indicators.note: a faulty item is defective, so the letters of grenade are set wrongly into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier handed a dud grenade is in mortal danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' and 'given' are link words joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger someone is to expose them to harm, so endangered means put at risk.

clue.text: Cheer overdue case being dismissed

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters; dismissing them leaves only the inside

parts.note: belated means late or overdue

explanation.surface: A defendant celebrates when a long-delayed court case is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case being dismissed' sounds legal; it means strip the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to make them very happy, a verb synonym of cheer.

clue.text: About to tuck into meal, ignoring starter he'd ruined

indicators.note: tucking into the meal puts the letter inside the word for the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter, which is left off

parts.note: he'd written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: He was about to dig into dinner but, skipping the first course, ruined it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' and 'tuck into' sound like dining but give mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it, like sinking a ship deliberately, so scuppered means ruined.

clue.text: Victoria's hubby maybe isn't PC tangling with coroner

indicators.note: tangling twists things together, so these letters become jumbled

explanation.surface: A police constable who is not getting along with the coroner.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Albert was famously given the title Prince Consort; 'maybe' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's husband Albert held the title, the husband of a reigning queen.

clue.text: Graduates penning article pronounced artist to be calculating individual

indicators.note: penning encloses, so the article is written inside the pair of graduates

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a graduate; two graduates give two of them
the is the definite article

indicators.note: pronounced signals going by how the artist's name is spoken rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: Art graduates writing a piece about a well-known painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian, said aloud, matches the ending -tician.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematician is someone whose work is numbers and calculation, a playful way of putting expert in maths.

clue.text: Writer shut up after considered point

indicators.note: after places the word for shut up behind the words before it

parts.note: felt means considered or believed
a tip is a point or end
to pen is to shut up an animal in an enclosure

explanation.surface: An author silenced after expressing a considered point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like silencing someone; here it means confined in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is an instrument for writing, and crosswords often call a pen a writer.

clue.text: Embarrass new copper with award hero essentially receives

indicators.note: receives means the middle letters of hero take the other pieces inside them
essentially picks out the essence of the word, its middle letters

parts.note: the middle two letters of hero
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A newly minted police officer with a medal is honoured, to his discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: An MBE is a British honour given in the monarch's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Encumber means to hamper or impede; embarrass has an older sense of hinder, as in financially embarrassed.

clue.text: Returning record label executive's first to come to office

indicators.note: returning means turning back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards
first points to the opening letter of the word executive's

parts.note: the opening letter of executive's
Decca is a famous British record label

explanation.surface: A former record label boss comes back to take up an office.
explanation.walkthrough: Decca is a record label whose roster ran from Pavarotti to the Rolling Stones.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede is to take up a post or throne, especially on succession, so it means attain a position of power.

clue.text: Nothing upset short fellow in Italy getting pasta

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word over so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A small man in Italy is undisturbed while being served pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the international car registration letter for Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is a type of flat, narrow ribbon noodle from Italy.

clue.text: Yank accepts place to put waste pipe

indicators.note: accepts means the word for yank takes the other word inside it

parts.note: to tug is to yank or pull sharply
a bin is where rubbish goes

explanation.surface: An American takes in a spot to dump rubbish through a waste pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American person; here it is the verb to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubing is lengths of tube, so a pipe or a run of piping.

clue.text: Signify agreement to interrupt live number

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the agreement word sits inside the others

parts.note: ten is a number
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Signalling assent to cut into a live song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live number' suggests a performance; the two words are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To betoken is to be a sign of something, so it means signify or indicate.

clue.text: Pupil ignoring current punishment

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the word for current

parts.note: discipline can mean punishment
in means current or fashionable

explanation.surface: A schoolchild who disregards the punishment they are currently serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts toward I, the physics symbol; here it is IN, meaning in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower who learns from a teacher, so a pupil or student.

clue.text: Peeping Tom frames European male head of government

indicators.note: frames means surrounds, so the snoop's letters enclose the others

parts.note: a prier is someone who pries, a snoop

explanation.surface: A voyeur sets up a European man and becomes a prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frames' can mean to set someone up for a crime; here it means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A premier is the prime minister, the leader of a government.

clue.text: Stubbornness from clubs during training seen to work

indicators.note: during puts the card suit's letter inside the rearranged letters
set to work, the letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Golf clubs seen in action at a practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the card suit clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigence is a refusal to compromise or change one's position, i.e. obstinacy.

clue.text: Fit Mike fools around

indicators.note: around means turned around, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
saps are fools

explanation.surface: Mike fools about and has a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is the noun for a sudden attack, not the adjective meaning healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary muscle contraction or a fit of something.

clue.text: Wanting answer, tried finding people in large crowd

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter for answer is dropped

parts.note: a court case that has been heard has been tried

explanation.surface: Without a solution, the officials tried to locate people in a vast crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' is legal: a case is heard in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The herd is the mass of common people, so people in a large crowd.

clue.text: Asian old man affectionately greeted Schwarzenegger, some said

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for one's father, the old man

indicators.note: some said means as spoken by some people, a homophone with a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: kissed means greeted affectionately, and Arnold Schwarzenegger is known as Arnie

explanation.surface: A father warmly greets Arnold Schwarzenegger, or so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the R of Arnie is silent, so the sounds match.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani is a person from Pakistan in South Asia, so an Asian.

clue.text: Suppose one needs space in retirement following work

indicators.note: following puts the work at the front, ahead of the pieces that follow it

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the word for space is read backwards

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a retiree needs a little room after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state or hold an opinion, so it means suppose or think.

clue.text: Square revolutionary fastening clasps

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters are read backwards
clasps means the word holds the answer within its letters

parts.note: the word fastening contains the needed letters in its middle, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A square revolutionary does up a buckle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun (a rebel such as Che) but here means turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a square number, three times three.

clue.text: Imbibing beer, team tends at intervals to become angry

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the beer word goes inside
at intervals means taking letters at regular spacing, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of team tends
bitter is a British type of beer

explanation.surface: When the team drinks beer, it often becomes bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British hoppy ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Embittered means resentful, filled with bitterness and anger.
